references.text: God gives Joshua the same promise that He will not let him go or forsake him, with almost identical wording as in Deuteronomy 31:6.
Joshua receives the same encouragement to be strong and courageous, and not to fear, because the Lord his God is with him.
David gives Solomon similar encouragement with words about being strong and courageous, and that God will not fail or forsake him.
God assures His people not to fear, because He is with them and will strengthen and help them.
The Lord promises to hold His servant's right hand and says, 'Do not be afraid; I will help you.'
God says, 'Do not be afraid, for I am with you' – the same theme of God's presence that removes fear.
Hebrews quotes directly from this promise: 'I will never leave you nor forsake you.'
Jesus promises to be with His disciples all days until the end of the world, reflecting God's promise of His presence.
